sentences.text: The writ petitioner seeks to quash the proceedings of the third respondent dated 06.03.2017 and the proceedings of the fifth respondent dated 20.08.2004, insofar it relates to the lands of the petitioner measuring 900 sq. m. in SF No.7/4A2, Vandiyur I-Bit Village, Madurai North Taluk, Madurai District.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that under a registered document bearing No.322/1993, she had purchased a vacant site measuring 22 cents comprised in S.No.7/4A2, Vandiyur I-Bit Village,
Madurai North Taluk, Madurai, and from the date of the purchase, she has been in effective possession and enjoyment of the same.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.

While so, respondents 1 to 3 had decided to widen NH 45B from Madurai to Trichy in furtherance to the Golden Quadrangle Scheme aimed at connecting all the National Highways from Kashmir to Kanyakumari.
Under the above scheme, the aforesaid land belonging to the petitioner was sought to be acquired.
The compensation was also paid as per the 5th respondent's proceedings dated 29.11.2006.

The petitioner would submit that possession of the lands have not been parted with and the lands lying to the north of the petitioner's land and north- east of the petitioner's land in Melamadai II-Bit and Vandiyur I-Bit have not been acquired.

The petitioner would submit that after she had collected the records through Right to Information Act, she came to learn that in respect of her lands, the acquisition proceedings have been initiated illegally.

The petitioner would further submit that there was no necessity for acquiring her land, as the lands lying on the east and west for forming National Highway has not even touched the northern boundary of Vandiyur I-Bit Village.
_ _ _ __ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.
While so, final notification was issued under Section 3B of the National Highways Act on 20.08.2004.
This notification, according to the petitioner, had not been served on her or any other land owners.

The petitioner therefore, sent a detailed representation to the respondents on 03.02.2017 along with a sum of Rs.30,580/-, which was the repayment of the compensation amount paid by the respondents to the petitioner.
The same was returned and thereafter, the third respondent passed an order dated 06.03.2017 stating that the lands belonged to the National Highways Authority.
The petitioner is therefore, before this Court challenging these orders.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the proceedings for widening the Ring Road Madurai from Meenakshi Mission Hospital to Kappalur was not part of the widening of the NH 45B Highway Road and therefore, since they had not parted with possession of the lands,
the respondents shall be directed to hand over the lands in question.
_________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would rely on an order of a learned Division Bench of this Court that relates to an other portion of the Highway in W.P.(MD) No.25947 of 2019 etc., dated 16.11.2022.

sentences.text: From the records that have been placed in the typed set of papers, there appears to be a communication dated 22.04.2017 issued by the third respondent, which is in reply to an RTI query.

The petitioner was informed that by letter dated 06.03.2017, the State Government has proposed to construct a flyover in the location and widen the service roads for which an NOC, which was sought for by the State Government has also been issued by the National Highways Authority of India in favour of the Highway Department to the Tamil Nadu State Government.

That apart, it has been brought to the notice of this Court that in a connected writ petition with reference to the acquisition proceedings in respect of the very same land and neighbouring lands, by order dated 15.12.2022 in W.P.(MD) No.2431 of 2015, a learned Judge of this Court had dismissed the writ petition.

The learned Judge had observed that for lands which are acquired as early as 2004 for which compensation has _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis been received in 2007, writ petition was filed 2015.
The learned Judge also observed that no power is vested with the Highways to drop the proceedings under the National Highways Act and consequently, the relief claimed was not maintainable.
The learned Judge has also taken note of the delay in approaching the Court.
After following the judgments, the writ petition was dismissed.
It is stated that a review is pending against the said order.
8. For the above reasons, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the orders passed by the third and fifth respondents.
Therefore, this Writ Petition is dismissed.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneouspetition is closed.
